evidence: Liv. 34.17.12: gravem atque opulentam cīvitātem, “a major and wealthy city” (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of size rather than weight, plain magnus is often enough (Lewis & Short: “important, of great weight, momentous”): magnum incommodum, a major problem.

evidence: Quint. 1.3.1: ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est
Tac. Dial. 28.4: cujus praecipua laus erat tuērī domum
Liv. 28.44.3: major ignōtārum rērum est terror
terms.comment: A comparative, not English “major”: urbs major is “a bigger town” (than some other), and majōrēs are elders or ancestors.

phrases.latin: ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est
phrases.english: in little children the major sign of talent is memory

sources: Lewis & Short: magnus (major) · Lewis & Short: gravis · Lewis & Short: praecipuus
